object_description: large three-storey building in the middle of a park with a monumental cascade staircase
design_condition: the perimeter is interpreted as a park with the large building at its centre, the sports fields on two sides at different levels forming the spatial connection to the adjacent residential areas

positive: The competition perimeter is interpreted as a park with a large building at its centre
The sports fields on two sides at different levels connect spatially to the residential areas
A monumental cascade staircase creates spaces at different levels using large terraces
The terrace in front of the main entrance continues indoors in the break hall
The prominently placed staircase runs through the entire building
The public uses along the break hall are coherently combined
The special uses and teacher areas beside the gymnasium are likewise coherent
The ground floor is spatially and organisationally attractive and promising
At first glance the upper classroom floor is a well-organised learning environment
Different and developable uses seem conceivable there
The building is gently placed into the existing topography
The main access via a wide staircase makes the entrance easy to find in the surroundings
A staggered sequence of spaces extends into the network of park paths
With a few measures a spacious outdoor space was created
Qualities lie in the urban precision, the generosity of the access figure and the entrance floor experience
The target values of ecological sustainability are met
negative: The cascade staircase ends somewhat abruptly in the grass field
The expectations raised by the ground floor are not fulfilled on the other floors
The outside staircase leads into long basement corridors past the cloakrooms
The lack of toilet facilities on the classroom floor is a serious deficiency
It is questionable whether 330 children can be supported without disruption in the learning landscape
The care rooms grouped inside prevent an overview of the floor and make orientation difficult
The structural concept above the gymnasium requires additional measures affecting the inner courtyards
There is no spatial-structural connection between the floors
The break hall idea, the gymnasium gesture and the differing plan typologies find no architectural expression
The restrained facade creates little identity and does not do justice to the public significance
The project is just below target costs partly because the school rooms are too small
Organising the entire school use on just one floor is problematic operationally
A project idea connecting the three main floors and a corresponding expression are missing
